answer: A healthy reef survives because every coral must anchor and grow in place, and an agent economy can borrow that rule: give each identity a beacon credential only after it locks a refundable stake and completes a history of real, verifiable work. Fresh identities start in a sable low-trust tier with strict caps on trades and voting weight, and graduate only when independent peers attest to repeated honest behaviour on a public ledger. Mass-producing fake agents then costs stake, time and reputation, while one honest history cannot be cheaply cloned.
